proof_summary: For a composite with an odd prime divisor \(q\), counting multiples of \(\operatorname{ord}_q(2)\) among the product factors and applying Legendre’s digit-sum formula gives strictly more \(q\)-adic valuation in the product than in \((n-1)!\), forcing \(q\mid a(n-1)\) and contradicting the hypothesis; the remaining case \(n=2^j\) is excluded by the exact computation \(v_2(a(2^j-1))=j-1\). Once \(n\) is prime, if \(\operatorname{ord}_n(2)<n-1\), then \(2^{\operatorname{ord}_n(2)}-1\) occurs in the defining product, so cancellation against \((n-1)!\) forces \(n\mid a(n-1)\), again contradicting the hypothesis; hence the order is \(n-1\).
